questions.q: According to this lesson, what is this course — and what is it explicitly not?
options: A complete beginner's course covering every Excel feature from scratch
A focused course on analyst-grade Excel (lookups, PivotTables, dynamic arrays, Power Query), not a 100-video 'Excel from zero' course
A course exclusively about Excel keyboard shortcuts
A course that assumes no prior spreadsheet experience of any kind
questions.explain: The course assumes basic Excel familiarity already and focuses on the specific analyst-grade tools: lookups, aggregation, PivotTables, dynamic arrays, and Power Query.

questions.q: What does the Name Box let you do?
options: Only displays the current date and time
Changes the font of the selected cell
Shows the selected cell's address and lets you jump instantly to any cell by typing its reference
Renames the entire workbook file
questions.explain: The Name Box, next to the formula bar, shows the current cell address and jumps you to any typed cell reference instantly — much faster than scrolling.

questions.q: What do Ctrl+Arrow and Ctrl+Shift+Arrow do?
options: Jump to (or select to) the edge of a contiguous data region, instead of scrolling through it manually
Open the Excel keyboard shortcuts reference dialog
Undo the last ten actions at once
Insert a new worksheet into the workbook
questions.explain: These shortcuts jump directly to where a contiguous block of data ends, replacing manual scrolling — one of the biggest everyday speed gains in Excel.

questions.q: What does pressing F4 do while editing a formula reference?
options: Toggles the reference between absolute and relative (e.g., $A$1 vs. A1)
Saves the workbook immediately
Converts the range into a PivotTable
Deletes the current formula entirely
questions.explain: F4 cycles a cell reference through its absolute/relative/mixed forms without retyping the dollar signs by hand.

questions.q: Why does this course start with a refresher chapter instead of jumping straight into PivotTables?
options: Because the refresher chapter is actually the hardest part of the course
To make sure everyone starts from the same interface/shortcut baseline before the analyst-grade material in later chapters
There is no reason — the ordering is arbitrary
Because PivotTables are being removed from later versions of Excel
questions.explain: Chapter 1 exists to establish a shared baseline (interface, shortcuts, tables, named ranges) before Chapter 2 moves into real analyst-focused functions.
